what.text: Refugees from Syria live in host countries including Türkiye, Germany, Lebanon, Jordan, and Iraq.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 2347756 refugees from Syria living in Türkiye.
In the same year, 668647 refugees from Syria lived in Germany.

why.text: The 2011 uprising in Syria led to the Armed conflict over the government of Syria active from 2011 to 2025, involving the Government of Syria against Syrian insurgents and the Military Council for the Liberation of Syria.

In the same period, Syria experienced the Armed conflict over Rojava Kurdistan territory, Syria active from 2012 to 2015 against PYD, and the Armed conflict with the Islamic State group, Syria active from 2013 to 2025 against IS.

Later active conflicts included the Armed conflict over the government and over Rojava Kurdistan territory, Syria active in 2016, 2018, and 2023 to 2025 against SDF, alongside the Interstate armed conflict between Israel and Syria active in 2025.

when.text: Displacement rose after 2011, with refugees from Syria in Türkiye reaching a year-end peak of 3737369 in 2021.
Key policy events occurred when Türkiye issued its temporary protection regulation in October 2014 and when the EU–Türkiye statement was agreed in March 2016.
After earthquakes in February 2023 and the fall of the Assad government in December 2024, return movements occurred and Türkiye hosted 2347756 refugees from Syria at the end of 2025.

how.text: Many Syrian refugees live in south-eastern Türkiye under Türkiye's temporary protection regulation, which sets out protection status rather than granting refugee status case by case.
The sources don't say which specific travel routes people used to reach host countries.
UNHCR counts these totals as registered refugees living in Türkiye at the end of each year.
